chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who performed Tawaf but became confused, saying: 'Did I do four circuits or did I do three circuits?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Which of the two Tawafs was it, an optional Tawaf or an obligatory Tawaf?' He said: 'If it was an obligatory Tawaf, let him throw what is in his hand and start anew; and if it was an optional Tawaf, and he is certain of three and in doubt regarding the fourth that he had circled, let him build upon the three, for it is permissible for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who is unsure if they completed three or four circuits of Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) applied to ritual doubt, distinguishing between obligatory and voluntary acts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for optional Tawaf, one may build upon the certain count (three) rather than restarting, whereas obligatory Tawaf requires a fresh start to ensure validity. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on certainty in fulfilling religious duties while providing ease in non-obligatory acts.
